assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly validated immuno-oncology target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical evidence. Five approved antibody drugs exist, over 1,700 ChEMBL IC50 entries are recorded, and 80 PDB structures including a sub-1Å resolution entry confirm deep structural characterisation. The target is well-established in cancer immunotherapy and continues to attract active research.
evidence_gaps: All five approved drugs are monoclonal antibodies targeting the extracellular domain; small-molecule druggability of the PD-1/PD-L1 interface remains more limited and challenging due to the flat protein-protein interaction surface
Resistance mechanisms to existing PD-L1 inhibitors are not fully characterised, limiting next-generation drug design
Predictive biomarkers beyond PD-L1 expression level for patient stratification remain incompletely defined
Intracellular signalling roles of CD274 (beyond immune checkpoint function) are less well characterised structurally
Small-molecule inhibitor data in ChEMBL, while present, may be dominated by tool compounds rather than clinical-stage molecules
